names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 23 iunie, «Sfântul Mucenic Aristocleu, preotul»; the form is the bare name, the rest of the line being rank and office.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 23 Ιουνίου, «Άγιοι Αριστοκλής ο πρεσβύτερος, Δημητριανός διάκονος και Αθανάσιος αναγνώστης», with the rank word left off.

death.note: doxologia.ro's life places his death in the persecution it dates «împăratului Maximian Galeriu (285-305)»; the interval is the reign the page prints, no closer year being given.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 23 iunie — «Sfântul Mucenic Aristocleu, preotul»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 23ης Ιουνίου — «Άγιοι Αριστοκλής ο πρεσβύτερος, Δημητριανός διάκονος και Αθανάσιος αναγνώστης»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 23 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and it is plainly the same man: the presbyter from Tamassos in Cyprus who hid in a cave on a mountain, came down to Salamis after a vision, and was beheaded with a deacon and a reader. Against the corpus's two other men of the name — Aristocles of Moscow and Aristokles the Athonite — the see and the century settle it. The page's heading reads «(; - 302)» and its narrative «Το 302 μ.Χ.», which falls inside the 285–305 bracket the folder's `dates` already carry, so no change to `dates` is proposed. The Greek line names his two companions, whom the corpus did not keep; they are new folders in the same day's batch. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence, and the page prints no hymn under their line.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue at pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).
